meta_description: How to request a copy of your data, correct it, export it or have it deleted from Onim, with the exact route for each request.
content:
This page is the practical half of the privacy policy: it lists the only personal data this site holds, and gives the exact steps to see it, correct it, export it or have it deleted. Every route ends in a person reading a message, not in a form that disappears.

What we hold about you — and what we do not

The complete list
CategoryHeld?Where it comes from
What you type into a calculatorNoStays in the page; gone when you leave.
Files you open in a toolNoProcessed in your browser; never transmitted.
Browsing history across other sitesNoNothing here can see it.
An account, password or profileNoThere are no visitor accounts.
Server log lines (IP, time, URL, browser)Yes, brieflyWritten automatically by the web server; rotated within about 30 days.
A contact message you sendYesName, email, optional phone, subject, message, IP, time.
A review you postYes, publiclyDisplay name, optional title, text, rating, time, shortened user-agent.
An anonymous like tokenYesA random string in the onim_vid cookie, plus the pages it has liked.

If something you are looking for is not in that table, the site does not have it. That is not a rhetorical claim: the code is written so that calculator inputs never reach a database and files never reach the server, which is why the list is this short.

Get a copy of what we hold

Send a message through the contact form with the subject Data request — copy. Include the email address you used when you wrote to us, and — if you posted a review — the display name and the page it is on. You will receive a plain-text summary of every record that matches: the message rows, the review rows and the like token if there is one. If nothing matches, we will say so explicitly rather than leaving you to guess.

You do not need to give a reason. A copy takes nothing more than the details above, and it is answered within 30 days, usually within a few.

Correct something

A typo in a review, a wrong name, a message you sent from the wrong address: send the correction through the form with the subject Data request — correction, quoting the page and what should change. Reviews are edited in place; a corrected review keeps a note that it was corrected only if the change alters what it says about a result.

Delete something

Three different things can be deleted, and the route is the same for all of them:

  • A contact message. Subject Data request — delete message, sent from the same email address you wrote from. The row is removed from the database, and the notification email in the team's mailbox is deleted with it.
  • A review. Subject Data request — delete review, with the page address and the display name on the review. The review is removed from the page and from the stored log. The page's count is adjusted at the same time.
  • A like. Subject Data request — reset likes. Clearing your browser's site data does this yourself, immediately, and is the faster route. If you want the server-side record cleared too, say so and it will be.

Deletion is carried out within 30 days and confirmed by reply. Two things cannot be deleted on request because they are not personal data: the daily page counters (a number and a date) and the ordinary server log lines older than the retention window, which no longer exist.

Opt out of everything at once

If you would rather not interact with any of it: do not press like, do not post a review, and do not send a message. Nothing else on this site stores anything about you. To remove the one cookie, clear site data for this domain in your browser; the site keeps working exactly as before.

Object or restrict processing

If you are in the EEA or the UK, you can object to processing based on legitimate interests — in practice, the server logs kept for security — and you can ask that a message or review be kept but not published while a question about it is resolved. Write to the same address with the subject Data request — objection and say what should stop. Because there is no marketing, there is no marketing opt-out to find: we do not send newsletters, and a contact message never adds you to a list.

Do not sell or share

We do not sell personal data and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising. There is no "Do Not Sell My Personal Information" link on this site because there is nothing to sell; that is a statement of fact about how the site is built, not a slogan.

Complaints

If you are not satisfied with how a request was handled, say so through the contact form first — the person who answers can fix most problems, including mistakes made in handling the request itself. If you are in the EEA or the UK you also have the right to complain to your national data-protection authority. We would rather you told us first, but the right exists regardless.

Two small practical notes

Verification. A request about a specific contact message is answered to the email address that sent it. That is the only check made, and it is what stops one person from deleting another person's message.

Reviews are public by design. If you post one and later want it gone, it will be removed on request. But until then it is visible to everyone who opens the page, so please do not put an email address, a phone number or anything else private into the text.
